overview:
Illinois' 16th District leans Republican by about 11 points, and incumbent Darin LaHood is seeking re-election after securing the Republican nomination. He enters the general election with roughly $6 million on hand, while Democrat Paul Nolley has raised about $639,000 but held only about $59,000 in cash, leaving a roughly hundred-to-one financial gap. No public general-election polling covers the race, and national race ratings do not list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give LaHood about a 96 percent chance of winning. The fundamentals point the same way: the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the fundraising disparity all favor LaHood. A national environment that has favored Democrats this cycle narrows his expected margin to roughly the mid-teens, short of the twenty-point spread the district's lean alone would imply. Nolley would need a dramatic shift in the political climate to make the race competitive.
